To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CORUM is a manually curated repository containing 2837 protein complex entries that are derived from a comprehensive set of 3198 different human genes.

CORUM 2 is a comprehensive resource of experimentally characterized mammalian protein complexes, that it is freely available, and that it can be accessed at the URL http://mips.helholtz-munehen.de/genre/projec/corum/index.html.

CORUM provides a manually curated database of mammalian protein-protein interactions that are grouped into protein complexes, that CORUM 2 is the most comprehensive database of mammalian complexes available and that CORUM 3 will be the first database that provides a comprehensive set of protein complexes that are experimentally characterized in a mammalian model system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of protein complexes in mammals.
the development of databases and tools to support the analysis of protein-protein interactions in the context of protein complexes.
the identification, characterization and analysis of protein complexes from mammalia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CORUM is the largest and most detailed publicly available database of mammalian protein complex information.
the new CORUM 2009 release is the most comprehensive resource of mammal protein complexes available.
CORUM is an excellent resource for researchers who want to get a comprehensive view of the mammalian protein complex landscape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CORUM database provides a valuable resource for researchers working with protein complexes in mammals.
CORUM is an excellent resource that is constantly being updated and improved.

CORUM 2 represents the most comprehensive and up-to-date repository of experimentally validated protein complexes for mammals, especially human, mouse and rat, which is freely available to the scientific community.
The main takeaway from our work is that

protein complexes are key functional units of the cell and their analysis is essential to understand the complexity of the proteome and to decipher the molecular mechanisms that underlie cellular processes.
CORUM is a valuable resource for the analysis of protein complexes, which will be of particular interest to systems biology and functional genomics studies. © 2010 IUPAC.

CORUM 2 is a valuable resource that provides a unique and comprehensive overview of experimentally determined protein complexes in mammalian organisms, which is a prerequisite for systems biological approaches.
